subject: We've limited your account
top_finding: A link points at a lookalike domain

message.subject: We've limited your account
message.excerpt: We noticed unusual activity and limited your PayPal account. Confirm your identity to restore access: https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=https-3A__paypa1-2Dsecure.example_confirm&d=DwMFaQ&c=abc

findings.title: A link points at a lookalike domain
evidence: Link to paypa1-secure[.]example reads like paypal[.]com once lookalike characters are folded (imitating PayPal)
findings.lesson: Hover before you click. The link's domain, not its text, tells you where you'll land.

findings.title: Sender domain imitates a known domain
evidence: Sender domain paypa1-secure[.]example reads like paypal[.]com once lookalike characters are folded (imitating PayPal)
findings.lesson: Read the domain letter by letter. Attackers register names that look right at a glance.

findings.title: Display name poses as a brand
evidence: Display name "PayPal Service" claims PayPal, sent from paypa1-secure[.]example
findings.lesson: The name on a message is free text. Check the address, not just who it says it is.

findings.title: Talks as a brand, links nowhere near it
evidence: Opens as PayPal but neither the sender nor any link uses a domain that belongs to it
findings.lesson: When a message says it's from a well-known company, go to that company's site yourself instead of using the link.
